caseno: Death Reference Case No. 64 of 2002 with Jail Appeal No. 666 of 2002.
lawyer:
Md Abdul Haque, State Defence Lawyer------ For the Condemned Prisoner. 
Golam Mohammad Chowdhury Deputy Attorney- General with Giasuddin Mitu, Assistant Attorney- General------ For the State.
parties:
State ------ Respondent 
Vs. 
Mukul @ Swapan ------ Respondent
full_judgment: 33. It appears from the record that the investigating Officer did not file the GD Entry dated 13-5-2002 which raises presumption under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act against the prosecution that had the GO Entry been filed it would go against the prosecution. Over and above, the learned Deputy Attorney-General could not offer any explanation for non filing of the GO Entry and also could not controvert the argument of the learned State Defence Lawyer regarding leaving of the police station by the police personnel for arrest of a dacoit without any command certificate and also in plain dress and even without any arms whatsoever. The prosecution also could not offer any explanation regarding non examination of Sub- Inspector A Bari, a vital witness in the case. All these facts creates a strong doubt about the truth of the prosecution story. It may be mentioned that it is in the evidence of the members of the raiding party that they did not raise any hue and cry at the time of occurrence but they have stated in their deposition that condemned prisoner Mukul was caught hold by the deceased and Mukul raised hue and cry as a result of which other accused persons rushed to the place of occurrence. It is therefore, significant that none of the witnesses from the place of occurrence village saw the injured Sub-Inspector Amzad at the place of occurrence or even heard about the occurrence. There is no evidence on record that anybody saw the raiding party at Chowgram village. The only local witness namely, PW 7, allegedly saw the other accused persons assaulting the village police with lathi and he did not see any police officer or victim Amzad. It is also important to note that according to the prosecution story, injured Amzad was brought from the place of occurrence to Singra Thana Health Complex by an engine-driven tempo but, curiously enough, the tempoo driver has not been examined in this case and none of the locality saw the victim at the place of occurrence or even the place of occurrence village. Thus, the natural presumption is that the victim might have received the injury elsewhere and the command certificate has been intentionally withheld by the prosecution.
